errors.english: the word "and so on" sets out the enumerated items
errors.why: གྲངས་ཅན here is most likely the Sāṃkhya: the 'and so on' brings in (cites) the Sāṃkhya position that [the universal] is colour etc., not 'the enumerated items'.

note: A close, careful rendering of a dense lemma-by-lemma commentary; only the Sāṃkhya reference is likely missed.

errors.english: Because they are the essence of what should and should not be done
errors.why: The gloss on karmapatha says they are 'karma' because they are of the nature of action and non-action (some of the ten are acts, some only paths of acts), not 'what should and should not be done'; the step 'they are also karma' is lost.

errors.english: visualize the qualities of the Buddha exactly as you have heard them described
errors.why: After the Buddha, the second object is 'the aspect as heard' (the Dharma), followed by the Saṅgha; the English makes it the Buddha's qualities again.

note: Fluent and largely faithful; one karmapatha gloss and the Buddha/Dharma/Saṅgha triad are slightly off.

errors.english: if the slander is not also untrue, then an offense is committed from the very beginning
errors.why: The Tibetan says the offense arises only if the slander, as above, is untrue.

fix.find: if the slander is not also untrue, then an offense is committed from the very beginning
fix.replace: only if the slander, as above, is untrue is an offense committed

errors.english: Reviling something like a mother [note: referring to the foundational texts or figures]
errors.why: མ here is the Mātṛkā (the third member after sūtra and vinaya), not 'a mother'.

fix.find: Reviling something like a mother [note: referring to the foundational texts or figures]
fix.replace: Reviling the Mātṛkā and the like

errors.english: If, after doing all this, the spirit still does not release its attachment
errors.why: The subject is the portents (འགྱུར་བ, the changes just listed): if they do not cease, the tree is not to be cut.

note: Readable, but the slander condition is inverted and the Mātṛkā is mistaken for 'a mother'.
The verses and the opening of the next jātaka are rendered faithfully in substance; some verse lines are loosely paraphrased.

errors.english: For those who are not already suffering, sufferings only increase further.
errors.why: It is upon those already suffering that sufferings increase (Skt. vyasaneṣv eva … vyasanodayāḥ).

fix.find: For those who are not already suffering, sufferings only increase further.
fix.replace: Upon those already suffering, sufferings only increase further.

errors.english: Being tormented by intense heat, the clouds did not send down rain.
errors.why: It is the people who are tormented by heat; the clouds did not rain on them (Skt. tapteṣu … na vavṛṣur ghanāḥ).

fix.find: Being tormented by intense heat, the clouds did not send down rain.
fix.replace: On those tormented by intense heat, the clouds did not send down rain.

errors.english: Following that sovereign, there arose another lord of the earth who ruled the land without interval.
errors.why: Skt. bhūmyanantaraḥ: a king whose land adjoins, i.e. a neighbouring king, not a successor.

fix.find: Following that sovereign, there arose another lord of the earth who ruled the land without interval.
fix.replace: That sovereign had a neighbouring lord of the earth, whose land bordered his.

errors.english: With his unbearable scepter of punishment [note: or taxes] and by seizing the property of all
errors.why: The line comparing his punishment to untimely death (Skt. akālakālakalpena) is not translated.

note: Covers the Tibetan verses (the interleaved Sanskrit is left untranslated), but the neighbouring king, the drought and the closing maxim are misread.

errors.english: that which can be established without relying on anything else
errors.why: བསྒྲུབ་ནུས་པ means the substance is able to accomplish (the two kinds of purpose) independently, not that it can be established.

note: Sound rendering of the substance/quality classification and the refutation of sound and odour as substances.

errors.english: if there is a distinction in the cause of existence
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་སྲིད་པ is 'as far as possible / accordingly' (parallel to ཇི་ལྟར་ཡོད་པ below), not 'the cause of existence'.

note: Follows the argument on body, transformation and consciousness correctly overall.

errors.english: "externalists" [note: original: "phyi rol pa rnams", likely referring to those who posit real universals outside the mind]
errors.why: The commentary itself glosses ཕྱི་རོལ་པ་རྣམས as 'what is external to the universal', i.e. the particulars, not non-Buddhist 'externalists'.

fix.find: "externalists" [note: original: "phyi rol pa rnams", likely referring to those who posit real universals outside the mind]
fix.replace: "the external ones" [note: i.e. what is external to the universal: the particulars]

errors.english: Due to the power of intense attachment
errors.why: ལྷག་པར་ཞེན་པ here is adhyavasāya, conceptual determination, not attachment.

fix.find: Due to the power of intense attachment

errors.english: This is taught because a conceptual mind
errors.why: ཞེས་བསྟན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ closes the previous sentence; the statement about the conceptual mind begins a new sentence and is not its reason.

errors.english: (bhavapada) an ontological entity
errors.why: དངོས་པོ is bhāva; 'bhavapada' is not the equivalent.

note: Argument largely followed, but key Pramāṇa terminology (adhyavasāya) and the 'external ones' are misread.

errors.english: Sanghadisesha
errors.why: This is the Mūlasarvāstivāda (Sanskrit) tradition: saṅghāvaśeṣa, not the Pali form.

errors.english: what is described here as "about to be emitted."
errors.why: What moves in the second moment is what is called 'has moved' (the just-emitted), not 'about to be emitted'.

errors.english: this ritual is for establishing the specific experience of pleasure
errors.why: ཆོ་ག here is the formulation of the rule, which specifies (for the case of intention) the experience of pleasure as a condition; it is not a 'ritual'.

note: Usable outline of a difficult Saṅghāvaśeṣa commentary, but the moment-distinction and Vinaya terminology need correction.

errors.english: "Holder of a Portion," evidently a powerful official,
errors.why: The Tibetan says nothing about who Dumbu Dzinpa is; 'evidently a powerful official' is the translator's unmarked guess.

fix.find: "Holder of a Portion," evidently a powerful official,

errors.english: yet that is a quality of the sapphire alone
errors.why: The verse argues virtue is not from birth: even when a glass bead takes on the sapphire's colour, that is its (the bead's) own quality; 'of the sapphire alone' inverts the point.

note: Good, readable rendering of the prose and verse; one unmarked interpretive addition.
